Course Description
❖This course is a continuation of the GEIT 1411 Computer 
Science I. It covers more advanced topics related to the Java 
programming language including inheritance, polymorphism, 
interfaces, exception handling, files and streams, generic 
collections, recursion and GUI components.
❖Integrated Development Environments (IDE)
IntelliJ IDEA (Community Edition), or
NetBeans
Download the IDE software on your computer and learn how to use it

slides.title: What will I Learn in this Course?

blocks.text: Towards the end of this course, you should be able to:
Describe objects and classes, class membership, and visibility modifiers
Apply inheritance and polymorphism in your code
Read and write data files and handle exceptions
Write recursive methods and think recursively

slides.raw_text:
What will I Learn in this Course?
❖Towards the end of this course, you should be able to:
Describe objects and classes, class membership, and visibility modifiers
Apply inheritance and polymorphism in your code
Read and write data files and handle exceptions
Write recursive methods and think recursively
Design abstract classes and interfaces
Develop communication and teamwork skills

slides.title: Is it Worth the Effort?

blocks.text: Object oriented programming is used everywhere
Simulation systems, games, flight simulators, etc.
Banking systems, business logic, and data processing
Developing applications for mobile devices and embedded systems
Creating tools and environments for software development

slides.raw_text:
Is it Worth the Effort?
❖Absolutely!
❖Object oriented programming is used everywhere
Simulation systems, games, flight simulators, etc.
Banking systems, business logic, and data processing
Graphical user interfaces
Dynamic and interactive web applications
Developing applications for mobile devices and embedded systems
Creating tools and environments for software development
